Title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
Action: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A318-111 and -112 airplanes; Model A319- 111, -112, -113, -114, -115, -131, -132, and -133 airplanes; Model A320-211, -212, -214, -216, -231, -232, and -233 airplanes; and Model A321-111, -112, -131, -211, -212, -213, -231, and -232 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes equipped with certain overhead stowage compartments (OHSC) bins. Investigations showed that bushings, retainer rings, and pins had migrated from their original positions. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection for discrepancies of affected OHSC bins and, depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: EPA is proposing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. Once finalized, the SNURs would require persons who intend to manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or process any of these chemical substances for an activity that is proposed as a significant new use by this rulemaking to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing that activity. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. markdown:
# Regulatory triage — SkyHop Airlines
Window 2026-11-02 → 2026-11-06 · as of 2026-11-06 · 2 items

## Critical (2)

- **Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes** [Federal Register]
  - Have maintenance check how many of our A319 and A320 jets need the proposed overhead bin inspection, estimate downtime and cost, and file comments if the proposal is impractical.
  - Dates: comment 2026-12-21 ✓ · Owner: Carlos Mendez (Director of Maintenance) · Areas: maintenance
  - 91 FR 69732 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22587/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes
- **Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations** [Federal Register]
  - Review the FAA's revised proposal on airport passenger ticket fees and submit comments if Denver or Salt Lake City fee collection and project approval changes would raise our costs or workload.
  - Dates: comment 2027-01-04 ✓ · Owner: Omar Haddad (Customer Policy) · Areas: customers
  - 91 FR 69511 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/04/2026-22450/update-and-clarification-of-the-passenger-facility-charge-regulations

votes.why: Plain English with a concrete next step: count affected jets, estimate impact, and comment if needed.
It calls the AD proposed, limits it to A319/A320, and makes no E175 or final-rule claims.
It covers the A319/A320 bin inspection and the comment date is shown, but it never says the inspection is one-time.
Understandable to a non-lawyer, with a clear step: review the proposal and comment if costs or workload rise.
Referring to 'fee collection ... changes' implies the proposal changes how airlines collect PFCs, which is a mustNotClaim.
It conveys the revised PFC proposal and airline fee collection, and the Jan 4, 2027 comment date is shown.
It gives Maintenance a concrete first step in plain English: count the A319 and A320 jets that would need the inspection.
It accurately describes the inspection as proposed and limits the review to A319 and A320 jets.
The card identifies the aircraft, the overhead bin inspection, and the comment deadline, but does not say the inspection is one-time.
It gives the owner a concrete next step: review the revised ticket-fee proposal for added costs or workload.
The phrase “fee collection and project approval changes” implies the proposal changes how fees are collected, which the rubric says not to claim.
The card conveys that this is a revised passenger ticket-fee proposal and shows the comment deadline, but does not say airlines collect the fees from passengers.
Plain-English instructions give the maintenance director a concrete assessment and comment workflow.
Accurately frames the AD as a proposal for A319/A320 aircraft without claiming it is final or covers E175s.
Omits the required point that the proposed check is a one-time inspection rather than recurring.
Clearly directs the owner in plain English to review the proposal and comment if warranted.
Refers to 'fee collection... changes,' violating the prohibition against claiming the rule changes how airlines collect PFCs.
Conveys the revised proposal on passenger ticket fees collected by the airline and displays the January 4, 2027 comment deadline.
